Keep patients from the server on this device
On: a patient you open from the server stays on this device and can be used offline. Off: the patient is removed from the device once you leave them; anything not yet sent is kept until it is sent.

On: every encounter you save gets its own visit, created for you. Off: you open a visit, record its encounters and end it yourself, like in OpenMRS, and a patient\'s encounters are shown grouped by visit.

Let other users see my registered data

Signed in as %1$s. Off by default. When off, other users who sign in on this device cannot see the patients you registered or downloaded here, unless they have access to them and download them themselves. When on, they can see them. This setting is yours only: each user has their own.

On: after you log in you go straight to the location you used last time. Off: you are asked for the location every time you log in. The location is yours only: another user who signs in on this device is asked for theirs.
These users have data on this device that has not reached the server yet. Log in as the user, then sync, to send it.

Answer the questions page by page (Next and Previous). The required ones must be filled in before you can go on, and the patient cannot be saved with data missing. Review your answers before submitting.

When patients were recorded to be identified later, this shows how many. What they hold is never sent by a sync until you identify them, so do it before syncing. It needs a signed-in user connected to the server; if the patient is not on the server you can register a new one, carefully.
Sign in and connect to the server to identify them.
Not on the server? Register a new patient

Register a new patient only if you are sure this patient is not in the system. Creating a new patient when they already exist creates a duplicate, which is hard to undo. Search again first, with other spellings, the identifier or the phone number.
